note: library = data + these rules. data/ is never edited. Each rule is mechanical, exact and counted: apply-library-fixes.mjs refuses to write unless the number of changes equals expectedCount, and source-scorecard.mjs re-applies the same rules to the originals in data/ (with separate code) and requires the result to equal library/. A change that is not listed here cannot pass gate 4.

rules.reason: The WEB conversion left a literal '> ' (an escaped markdown quote marker for the first line of a poem) at the start of 117 Psalm verses. It is formatting, not scripture. The Worker was supplying it to the model inside quoted scripture.

rules.reason: Literal HTML entities left in the text by the markdown conversion (141 Psalm chapters). The same file already uses the real em dash 796 times, so this makes it consistent. Meaning unchanged.

pairs: <<
>>
rules.reason: The postscript printed after 1 Corinthians 16:24 ("written from Philippi by Stephanas...") is wrapped in the HTML entities for << and >>. They become the guillemets « and »: decoding to << and >> would collide with the Worker's own >>SCRIPTURE and >>COMMENTARY block markers. Wording unchanged.
2 John has one chapter. The notes are stored under the key "5". Their paragraphs are numbered 1 to 13 and 2 John has 13 verses, so the key becomes "1". Text unchanged.

Wesley's notes on Leviticus 1 sit at the end of the book introduction (no chapter 1 entry). CCEL's copy has the same text in the same order inside its "Introduction to Leviticus and Chapter I" section. The text from the chapter's own summary line ("Directions concerning burnt-offerings...") to the end becomes chapter "1"; the introduction keeps everything before it. No words changed.

Three chapters held text that belongs elsewhere. (1) Psalms: the notes on Psalms 100-150 sit on the end of chapter 99 (61,862 characters). They are split into chapters 99-150 at each psalm's own first line, using our own text (same spelling and line breaks as the rest of Wesley here); this replaces the 51 CCEL-sourced chapters that an earlier change (merged Oct 31, rule wesley-psa-100-150-from-ccel) added on the mistaken belief that Psalms 100-150 were missing; that rule and its patch file are retired, and each replaced chapter must match its recorded hash. (2) Malachi 4: the book's scripture index (23,722 characters) was appended after the last note; cut. (3) Revelation 22: Wesley's Old Testament preface (17,417 characters) was appended after the last note; cut. The cut text stays in data/. Cut points and hashes are in the patch file.

In 544 places our Wesley text has lost the dash that follows his headword ("Multiplied Which forced..." for "Multiplied - Which forced..."). Each place is listed in the patch file where CCEL's copy of the same work has a lone dash between two words that are identical in ours and nothing else differs at that spot. The patch records each chapter's sha256 before and after; the tool and, separately, the scorecard re-check them.

In Zechariah (14 chapters), Malachi (4), 1 Timothy (6), 2 Timothy (4) and Titus (3) our copy holds only 6-10% of each chapter (for example Zechariah 71,392 characters against 878,861 in CCEL's copy of the same translation). Every 6-word run of our text is found in the CCEL chapter (at least 97% in every chapter replaced; the patch records the figure), so ours is a shortened copy, not different wording. The 31 chapters are replaced with CCEL's full chapter text (tags and footnotes removed, as in our copy). Each entry carries the sha256 of our text before and of the new text after, and the tool refuses any chapter that matches neither. Source: CCEL calcom30.xml and calcom43.xml (hashes recorded in the patch folder note).

In our Calvin copy a chapter commonly ends with the opening verse block of the next chapter (for example 1 Corinthians 3 ends with 'CHAPTER 4 1 Corinthians 4:1-5 ...') and lacks its own; the first chapter of a book lacks its opening block altogether; and Philemon carries 3,000 characters of another book's scripture translation after its last paragraph. CCEL's copy of the same translation has every chapter whole. A chapter is replaced with CCEL's only if at least 97% of our chapter's 6-word runs are found in CCEL's chapter or the next (nothing of ours is lost) and at least 97% of CCEL's chapter is found in ours or its neighbours (nothing is invented). The patch records both figures for every chapter, the sha256 of our text before and of the new text after. 136 chapters failed the test and are left alone (Isaiah 1-66 and Acts 1-28 among them: Isaiah volumes 13-16 lack chapter headings in CCEL, and our Acts text carries material CCEL does not); they are listed for later review.

Our copy of Matthew Henry drops every poetry and Latin quotation that sits on its own lines in the printed text, with its attribution (for example the Blackmore verses after Job 1:4 and the Latin of Horace and Virgil in Acts, Isaiah and Romans), and one list: the subject index at the end of Proverbs 31. CCEL's copy has them (they are <verse> and <ol> elements). 75 blocks in 60 chapters are inserted as their own paragraphs after the paragraph that precedes them in CCEL. Each chapter's text before and after is recorded by sha256 in the patch, and each insertion place is checked against the text around it. Nothing in our text is changed or removed.

In the first Calvin repairs, text that our copy had at the end of the wrong chapter was dropped when chapters were replaced from CCEL, and some of it was Calvin's own: his Preface to Lamentations, Zephaniah and Haggai, and 29 chapter-opening Scripture tables (English and his Latin). The same kind of text still sits at the end of the previous book in ten places (Calvin's Prefaces to Obadiah, Micah and Nahum, and the Arguments for James, 2 Peter, 1 John, Jude, Ephesians, Colossians and 2 Thessalonians). 42 blocks are moved to the start of the chapter they belong to (13 prefaces and arguments to chapter 1 of their book, 29 tables to their own chapter), and the ten tails are cut from where they were. The text is from our own copy; nothing is retyped. CCEL is the witness: at least 95% of each block is found in CCEL's files (recorded per block in the patch). Each chapter's text before and after is recorded by sha256, and each cut records the offset, length and sha256 of the text removed. Left out on purpose: the 43-word editor's note and the translation of Jeremiah 52 (no commentary), and the translator's prefaces, dedications and other front matter that CCEL has and our copy never had (a separate decision).

Calvin opens Acts 4 (339 words) and Acts 8 (135 words) with a short argument before the first Scripture passage. Our copy never had them: neither data/ nor library/ holds the text (the footnote [201] that belongs to the Acts 4 argument was there, so the argument was dropped, not absent from the book). CCEL has them. Each is added at the start of its chapter, taken from CCEL's own paragraph, with the footnote marker [201] our copy uses. The other 26 chapters of Acts open with their Scripture passage and need nothing. The roughly 3-5% by which our Acts is longer than CCEL's is the translator's footnotes (Latin phrases with English glosses), which our copy keeps inside the chapter text and CCEL keeps as separate notes: genuine content, nothing to remove.

Found by scanning every chapter pair for text repeated at the end of one chapter and the start of the next. Seven chapters of Calvin end with text that the next chapter already holds: the opening Scripture table of the next chapter in Genesis 1, Genesis 24, Joshua 1, 2 Thessalonians 1 and Ephesians 1 (96 to 1,303 words) and, in Amos, the end of chapter 2 (86 words, chapter 3's table) and all of chapter 2 at the end of chapter 1 (10,809 words, 98.5% found in chapter 2). The cause was an earlier restore from CCEL, whose Amos 'Chapter 1' division also holds chapter 2 (there is no chapter 2 heading), and which left the original tail in place beside the restored opening. Each tail is cut from the chapter it does not belong to; the same text stays in the next chapter, so nothing is lost. Every cut is checked by offset, length and sha256, and the builder refuses a case unless at least 98% of the cut text is found in the next chapter. The only text that exists nowhere else is the 162-word English and Latin translation of Amos 2:1-3 inside the Amos 1 tail, which belongs with the translations noted in the open issue calvin-chapter-opening-translations. Not touched: Exodus 11 (a 44-word run that is a quotation shared with chapter 12) and Ezekiel 12 (a tail of back matter, handled separately).

Twelve chapters of Calvin ended with the back matter of a CCEL volume that our original scrape appended to the last chapter of the last book in that volume: Calvin's own translation of the book(s) in the volume (Galatians and Ephesians; Habakkuk, Zephaniah and Haggai; Hosea; Jeremiah 1-47 in four parts; Joshua; 1 Peter; Jonah, Micah and Nahum; Joel and Amos; Romans), a CCEL placeholder sentence in Hosea 14, and the first lines of the volume's index of scripture references in Haggai 2 (47,113 words in all). None of it is commentary on the chapter it was found in. It is cut from the commentary and kept, word for word, in library/held/calvin-held.json with where it was found, why it was cut, a classification and a hash. The tool refuses to cut a tail unless the held items add up to exactly the text being cut, so nothing can be removed without being kept. The translations are a separate content type (see the open issue calvin-chapter-opening-translations); where they finally belong is not decided.

Ezekiel 12 ended with the opening Scripture table of Ezekiel 13 (Lecture Thirty-Fourth, Ezekiel 13:1-3, English and Latin), which Ezekiel 13 already holds. The tail is cut; the same text stays in Ezekiel 13, so nothing is lost. The cut is checked by offset, length and sha256, and the builder refuses it unless at least 98% of the cut text is found in Ezekiel 13.

rules.countLabel: volume title pages held and cut
rules.reason: The end of Ezekiel 12 carried the title page of the next CCEL volume ('Commentaries on the First Twenty Chapters of the Book of the Prophet Ezekiel ... Volume Second ... Christian Classics Ethereal Library ... www.ccel.org'), 47 words. It is front matter, not commentary. It is cut and kept word for word in library/held/calvin-held-volume-matter.json.

Thirteen chapters of Calvin carry the back-matter indexes of a CCEL volume that our original scrape put inside them: the index of scripture references in all thirteen, the index of Greek words (2 Corinthians 13, Ezekiel 12, John 21), Hebrew words (Ezekiel 12, and a heading in John 21) and Latin and French words (Ezekiel 12), and a CCEL placeholder sentence in Ezekiel 12. Eleven sit at the end of the chapter; two (Luke 19 and Numbers 10) sit in the middle, with Calvin's commentary carrying on after them, so the text before and after is rejoined with a blank line. 6,401 words in all (all classes: index, placeholder, title page), none of it commentary. Each section is cut and kept word for word in library/held/calvin-held-volume-matter.json with where it was found, why it was cut, a classification and a hash. The tool refuses to cut unless the held items add up to exactly the text being cut.

The end of Colossians 4 repeated the opening Scripture table of 1 Thessalonians 1 ('Commentary on the First Epistle of Paul to the Thessalonians. Chapter 1 ... 1 Thessalonians 1:1', English and Latin, 76 words), which 1 Thessalonians 1 already holds. The tail is cut; the same text stays in 1 Thessalonians 1, so nothing is lost. The cut is checked by offset, length and sha256, and the builder refuses it unless at least 98% of the cut text is found in 1 Thessalonians 1.

'Argument on the First Epistle to the Thessalonians' (Calvin's summary of the epistle) sat at the end of Colossians 4 because our original scrape ran the end of the Colossians volume section into the next book. It belongs to 1 Thessalonians and is moved to the start of 1 Thessalonians 1, as the Arguments of other books were placed at the start of their first chapter by calvin-move-front-matter-and-chapter-openings. The builder refuses the move if this text is already anywhere in 1 Thessalonians; the cut and the added text have the same sha256.

Calvin's two dedicatory epistles sat at the ends of the chapters before the commentaries they open: the dedication to Matthurinus Corderius (Geneva, 17 February 1550) at the end of Colossians 4, and the dedication to Benedict Textor (Geneva, 1 July 1550) at the end of 1 Thessalonians 5. In the CCEL volume each is the 'front' division 'Calvin's Dedication' of 'Commentary on First Thessalonians' and 'Commentary on Second Thessalonians'. They are moved to the start of 1 Thessalonians 1 and 2 Thessalonians 1, in the same way other front matter was moved. The 'End of the Commentary on ...' lines stay where they are. The cut and the added text have the same sha256.

In Jonah, Micah and Nahum the English and Latin Scripture table that opens a chapter (143 to 886 characters, e.g. 'Chapter 2. Jonah 2:1-2 ...') sat at the end of the chapter before it, as an earlier restore from CCEL had left it. Eleven tables (Jonah 2-4, Micah 2-7, Nahum 2-3) are moved to the start of their own chapters, which is where the other chapters of Calvin have them. The builder refuses a move if the table is already at the start of the next chapter; each cut and its added text have the same sha256.

Our Calvin Psalms are a shortened copy: every Psalm stops after roughly the first 1,000-2,500 words (about 126,000 words for all 150, against about 804,000 in CCEL's copy of the same translation, volumes 8-12). Every 6-word run of our text is found in CCEL's Psalm (at least 97% in every Psalm replaced; the patch records the figure for each), so ours is a shortened copy, not different wording. 148 Psalms are replaced with CCEL's full text (tags and footnotes removed, as in our copy); Psalms 70 and 108 were already complete. Psalm 119 also carried the title page and translator's preface of volume five in the middle of its text (about 1,150 words); they are CCEL front matter, not commentary, so the replacement does not include them. The patch records their sha256 and word count, and the original file in data/ keeps them. openIssues.location: ISA 1-16 measured (16 chapters, about 14,800 words); about 240 chapters in 26 books estimated, provisional
openIssues.description: Chapter-opening translations: CCEL contains Calvin's translation of the biblical chapter, generally with Latin alongside English. These blocks are absent from the repository copy. Comparison of Isaiah 1-16 found no missing commentary; the large word-count difference is explained by these translations and by translator footnotes retained in the repository copy. Do not treat the translations as missing commentary or merge them into commentary text. Revisit as a separate content type when designing the comparison-site schema. Estimated occurrence across Calvin's corpus (about 159,000 words) comes from an earlier comparison that pre-dates some repairs and remains provisional pending complete volume coverage. If imported later, they are newly sourced CCEL translation material and need their own provenance and rights review: they are in neither data/ nor library/.
openIssues.notFixedBecause: the translations are a different content type from commentary; adding them to the chapter text would distort verse-level comparison, and no field for them exists yet.

openIssues.description: 15 literal HTML entity sequences ('<' x3, '>' x6 and '&' x4 as counted by the scorecard in these chapters), mostly inside garbled Greek transliteration (e.g. 'de< pro<v'), double-encoded from an older Greek encoding. CCEL's copy has the same garbling in Genesis 47; the chapters it replaced (GEN 46, EZK 14, JHN 12 and others) no longer show it.
openIssues.notFixedBecause: Decoding the entities would not recover the Greek; the passage needs a clean copy of the Greek, not a text substitution.
